chunks: They regard the Master of the Throne as the store for the day of their need,
and they turn to Him when the creation turns to the creatures, out of their love (for Him),
they do not reach the ending limit of His worship,
nor does frivolity turn them away from adhering to His obedience,
except to springs in their hearts that are never devoid of His hope and His fear,
fear never leaves them so that they might slacken in their efforts,
nor have temptations entrapped them so that they might prefer this light search over their (serious) effort.
They do not consider their past (virtuous) deeds as big,
for if they had considered them big then fear would have wiped away hopes from their hearts,
ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the righteous regarding their worship and reliance on God?
ai.summary: In this passage from the 'Al-Ashbaah' chapter, Imam Ali (AS) characterizes the elite of the righteous (al-awliya) who treat Allah’s Throne as their ultimate refuge during existential crises. Their spiritual equilibrium is maintained by a persistent balance of hope (rajā’) and fear (khawf), preventing them from falling into either the complacency of self-satisfaction or the despair of neglect. This state ensures their worship remains sincere and their efforts consistent, anchored in the conviction that divine mercy outweighs their shortcomings.
